expectedEvidence.statement: Student rewrites the concern as a symptom statement naming conditions, frequency and an observable effect.
expectedEvidence.notes: A statement such as 'rough running reported under highway acceleration, intermittent, warning lamp reported' is sufficient.

expectedEvidence.statement: Student lists the unknown vehicle and system information and states why each item matters.
expectedEvidence.notes: Make, model year, engine and system are the expected core items.

expectedEvidence.statement: Student states that a verified service-information source is required and refuses to guess a specification.
expectedEvidence.notes: This is the central lesson of the week given the unavailable service-information asset.

expectedEvidence.statement: Student provides an ordered plan in which each step names the observation that would confirm or refute a hypothesis.
Student discloses at least one assumption and what would confirm or refute it.
expectedEvidence.notes: Expected for full marks but not required to pass the exercise formatively.

acceptableAlternatives.statement: Any plan order is acceptable if each step is justified and its decision point is stated.
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Do not treat a particular sequence as the correct answer.

acceptableAlternatives.statement: Students may propose asking the customer, inspecting the vehicle, or consulting a verified source first, provided they justify the choice.

misconceptionFeedback.misconception: The customer's description can be treated as a verified symptom.
misconceptionFeedback.feedback: A customer report is subjective and unverified. Ask what observation would confirm the concern and how it would be recorded.

misconceptionFeedback.misconception: A plan can proceed without knowing the vehicle.
misconceptionFeedback.feedback: Without make, model year and engine, no manufacturer information applies and no test can be justified against it. Ask which unknowns must be closed first.

misconceptionFeedback.misconception: An unverified online reference can be used as authority.
misconceptionFeedback.feedback: Unverified sources cannot establish a specification. Ask what would make a source acceptable and who would have to approve it.

debriefPrompts: Which unknown, if resolved, would most change your plan?
Where did you state a need for information instead of inventing it?

sources.title: Service information source (not available, rights unverified)
sources.notes: Instructors must not supply unverified service information to complete this lab.

technicalReviewChecklist.statement: Guide supplies no manufacturer procedure or specification.
Expected evidence is reachable from the student materials.
Feedback does not assert a vehicle condition.
No answer content appears in the student bundle.
